An unresolved mandatory pin rejects the candidate catalog (fail-closed is intended); the previously published catalog keeps serving. Every pin-failure record states whether it BLOCKED publication (candidate rejected) or left a degraded candidate publishable.
- R21 (owner rulings 2, 3, 4, 13): A failed pin check reports EVERY unresolved pin — never only the first — each with its safe server and tool identity (R8-validated) and its configuration source location (file, property path, one-based line, one-based column). A pin whose server discovery failed is reported as UNVERIFIABLE with the shared discovery cause, never as tool-absent; only a successful, complete tool listing establishes absence. For each affected server the actually discovered tool names are listed (affected servers only, never healthy servers), split across bounded records sharing the refresh correlation ID, server ID and chunk index/count, with no silent truncation. Every failed pass repeats its complete details — no deduplication, no reference t…
- R22 (owner rulings 6, 7, 11, 12, 14, 15): Logs alone are the diagnostic path: an operator identifies all blockers, the configuration revision used, and the catalog still being served without consulting metrics or `/readyz`. Every refresh pass emits start and outcome records sharing one correlation ID, stating the configuration revision, the trigger, and the next scheduled attempt. A failed pass distinguishes the retained catalog (generation, tool count, age) from no-usable-catalog/zero-upstream-tools, and distinguishes candidate counts from retained counts. A successful refresh emits an explicit completion summary with COUNTS ONLY — servers discovered, tools discovered, tools published, mandatory pins resolved out of total — and never per-server or per-too…
- R23 (owner rulings 8, 9): An upstream discovery failure names the failing stage — closed set `dns|connect|tls|auth|initialize|tools_list` — with a bounded cause category and the HTTP status or timeout value where applicable. The endpoint appears sanitized as scheme/host/port/path only; never credentials, headers, query strings, or bodies (R8). Each failure states its recovery expectation — automatic retry scheduled vs configuration/credentials require correction — with the next attempt time, and after a rejected pass the affected server's readiness reason is non-empty and identifies the failure, distinct from not-yet-probed.
- R24 (owner rulings 10, 18): The log shows a configuration edit reaching the running process: reload attempts identify the configuration revision and trigger and whether the candidate was accepted or rejected; refresh records name the revision they used. Startup, SIGHUP reload and periodic refresh report IDENTICAL pin diagnostic detail — identity, source location, discovery evidence, publication impact, retry guidance; no path is the only way to obtain the useful error.
- R25 (owner rulings 16, 17): All pin/refresh diagnostics appear at DEFAULT log levels; no failure diagnostic is debug-only. Defects in the logging path itself are surfaced as a minimal credential-free fallback record rather than failing silently.
- Non-goals (r8): the wider configuration-failure logging audit is DEFERRED (owner scope ruling "lets just focus on pins"); no new metrics; no induced-failure review gate (owner judges sufficiency during normal deployment, ruling 19).
